ops.title: Test leaks: kill/reap-path tests orphan live processes on abnormal runs (yasyf box evidence)
ops.description:
The yasyf box pre-repair sweep (2026-07-25, no reboot since Jul 19) found leaked Go-test child processes surviving days after the swarm-era test runs that spawned them died:

- 2× `verifier-child` from `TestProcessVerifierCancellationReapsAndReusesDedicatedLane` (daemonkit `trust`), reparented to PID 1, elapsed ~1d20h, idle.
- 1× busy-wait `sleep 0.01` loop from `TestCmdTransportResetKillsBackgroundedDescendant` (~51 min CPU) and 2× from `TestBridgeRecoveryReapsLeaderlessGroupBeforeReceiptAcknowledge` (~18 min CPU each), together burning ~14% of a core continuously since Jul 23/24. (Locate these two tests by grep — they may live in a downstream repo rather than daemonkit itself.)

The irony is the finding: these are precisely the tests that claim to prove kill/reap/cancellation behavior, and their children outlived the suite when the run was killed externally (swarm kill / machine load). Same failure flavor as the claude-pool `...DeadlineKillsReapsAndUntracks` orphaned daemonkit-worker (separate investigation). Processes were evidence-captured to a file on the box and then killed during the sweep; the ps capture is in the sweep report attached to the machine-repair task thread (fc39f885).

Worth deciding: should test-spawned children carry a parent-death signal (PDEATHSIG equivalent on darwin — kqueue EVFILT_PROC watch, or a stdin-pipe-EOF exit convention) so an externally killed test binary can never strand them? The stdin-EOF convention is the portable shape daemonkit already uses elsewhere in the spawn path.

ops.text: reproduce: kill a running test binary mid-test (SIGKILL) for each named test and demonstrate the child exits on its own within a bounded window
fix landed so test-spawned helper children exit when the test binary dies without cleanup
no leaked verifier-child or busy-wait helper after a killed run of the affected suites
